values.description:
Nullable: an entry is null where the scrape did not report that series,
which is a gap rather than a measurement of zero. A generated client that
types these as plain numbers will reject the first gap it meets.

Said here rather than declared in the schema because swaggo cannot mark an
array's items nullable — x-nullable lands on the array, which would claim
the column itself may be null, and that is a different and untrue thing.

truncated.description:
Truncated says the trace held more records than one response carries. It is
reported rather than silently applied, because a waterfall drawn from a cut
record set is wrong in a way nothing in the picture reveals.

attrs.description:
Attrs is whatever the runtime attached to the log call, passed through as it
sent it. swaggertype keeps the description honest about that: bytes to Go,
arbitrary JSON to a client.

cost_usd.description:
CostUSD is what could be priced and UnpricedCalls how many calls could not
be. They are reported side by side because the total alone is a lower bound
whenever the second is non-zero, and a reader with only the first has no way
to know that.

dropped_records.description:
DroppedRecords is how many records the publisher admitted losing in this
window. It is per app and never per trace: the marker carries no trace id,
so nothing can say which traces are incomplete — only that some are.

integration_id.description: IntegrationID is empty when the deployment could not be resolved to one.

deployment_ids.description:
DeploymentIDs is every deployment that contributed records. More than one
means the trace crossed apps: the id rides on the message and survives a
queue hop, so this is how a reader learns the trace is not one app's story.

body.description:
Body and Vars are null when the runtime captured no payload AND when the
caller asked for the trace without them. The two are indistinguishable here
by design: a client that asked for no bodies knows it did.
swaggertype says what RawMessage means on the wire: bytes to Go, arbitrary
JSON to a client. Without it the description would call these base64 strings.
Their shape belongs to the block that was traced, not to this API.

cache_write_tokens.description:
CacheWriteTokens is cache creation, billed above the input rate. NULL only
when the record carried no usage at all (including every record written
before the column existed); 0 when a provider reported usage but no write
count, which is every provider but Anthropic.

dropped.description:
Dropped marks a record the runtime shipped as incomplete; Truncated marks
one whose payload was cut to fit.

info.description:
The platform's stored telemetry: log events and the traces beside them,
as shipped by deployed runtimes and stored in Postgres.

The service is called "logs" everywhere — the binary, the image, the pod
and the LOGS_URL other services reach it by — but it stores traces too.
They landed here because they are the same shape of problem, so one
description covers both.

This is an in-cluster service and performs no authentication of its own.
It is ClusterIP in the chart and the platform BFF is the authorization
boundary in front of it. Every query route is a read; the three
retention routes are the exception, and one of them deletes stored
telemetry — so anything that can reach this address can erase it as
well as read it. Keep it internal.
info.title: Octo Logs API

get.description:
Answers as soon as the process is serving, whether or not Postgres or
NATS are reachable — it is what the readiness probe polls while the
rest is still coming up.

One page of stored log events, newest first. Every filter is optional and
they combine; a page that came back full carries next_before, which is the
cursor to send as before= for the page after it.

get.description:
This API as an OpenAPI 3.1 document. Narrow it with tag or path — the
full document is mostly schemas, and a filtered one carries only the
schemas its operations can reach. The two filters are alternatives, not
a combination.

parameters.name: tag

parameters.description: Keep only routes starting with this prefix
parameters.name: path

get.description:
Every route as one line: method, path, summary and tags. Read this
first to find the tag or path worth asking the description about.

post.description:
Deletes what the stored policy no longer keeps and reports how much went.
This is what the chart's nightly job calls. A policy that keeps everything
is a 200 with zero counts and null cutoffs rather than an error — being
asked to do nothing is an answer.

A trace is deleted whole: its records go with its summary, so a swept trace
never becomes one that lists but cannot be opened. Stored model prices are
never swept, because a traced call's cost points into that history.

get.description:
How many days of log events and of traces this installation keeps. Zero on
an axis means keep forever, which is the default — an installation that has
never configured retention reads back as zeros rather than as an error.

oneOf.description: The two retention windows, in days. Both are required

requestBody.description: The two retention windows, in days. Both are required

400.description: a window is missing, negative, or beyond 3650 days

get.description:
The catalogue, built from the pods' dictionaries alone — no samples are read.
It exists so a caller can find exact metric names before asking for data,
which is what makes the required metric filter on the series route usable.

Label sets are nested under their metric name. One histogram is a single
entry with a series per bucket boundary, rather than a hundred names that
happen to share a prefix.

truncated means the pod list hit its cap, so the catalogue is partial: a
metric missing from it may simply belong to a pod that was dropped.

parameters.description: The deployment to describe
parameters.name: deploymentId

parameters.description: Only these pods; repeat the parameter for more than one
parameters.name: pod

parameters.description: Only metrics whose name starts with this
parameters.name: prefix

get.summary: List the metrics a deployment exposes

get.description:
Every pod of the deployment the stats index still holds, most recently seen
first. Read this first: it names the pods the other two routes accept, and
says whether each is still reporting.

liveRows and rollupRows are reported separately on purpose. Zero live rows
beside a full history is the ordinary state of a pod that stopped a few hours
ago, because the live tier is kept for only twice the rollup interval while
the pod stays in the index for the whole retention window.

An unknown deployment answers 200 with no items rather than 404. This service
holds no deployment registry, so it cannot tell a deployment that never
existed from one whose sidecar is switched off or whose stats have expired.

parameters.description: The deployment to describe
parameters.name: deploymentId

get.summary: List the pods reporting stats for a deployment

get.description:
Points for the named metrics, per pod, decoded against each pod's dictionary.

metric is required, and repeatable. It is what bounds the response: the rows
are stored positionally, so a query with no name filter would read every
series of every pod. Use the metrics route to find the names.

A counter's value is its growth over the interval ending at that point, on
both tiers, so a chart does not have to know which tier answered. Its closing
cumulative reading is available as the last stat on the rollup tier, and
counters=absolute returns the raw readings instead. A counter that went
backwards is treated as a process restart rather than a negative delta.

tier=auto picks live when the window fits inside the live tier's reach and
rollup otherwise, because a window older than that cannot be answered from
live rows however many are read. The resolved tier and its step are echoed
back.

times are unix milliseconds, oldest first, and the columns are parallel. A
null value is a gap rather than a zero. On the rollup tier ends is carried
too, because rows are not contiguous: when a bucket's end does not meet the
next one's start, scraping had stopped in between.

parameters.name: deploymentId

parameters.name: metric

parameters.name: label

parameters.name: pod

parameters.name: tier

parameters.name: from

parameters.description: End of the window, RFC3339. Defaults to now
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: Which numbers to return, comma separated: value, min, max, last, samples. Rollup tier only
parameters.name: stats

parameters.description: delta for growth, absolute for the raw cumulative reading
parameters.name: counters

parameters.description: Points per series, clamped to 1..5000
parameters.name: limit

400.description: no metric was named, a time is not RFC3339, or a parameter is not one of its values

combine; a page that came back full carries next_before, which is the cursor
to send as before= for the page after it.

reaches back as far as the store goes.

get.description:
Every app that ran a trace in the window, with its counts and cost. Read this
first to find the app worth listing traces for.

The window is echoed back in the response, because the caller may not have
chosen it and every count is meaningless without it. Either bound may be given
alone: from with no to reads to now, and to with no from reads back 24 hours.

parameters.description: Start of the window, RFC3339. Defaults to 24h before to
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: End of the window, RFC3339. Defaults to now
parameters.name: to

400.description: a time is not RFC3339, or to is before from

get.description:
One trace: the summary the list already showed, plus every record that fed
it, in sequence. The summary is the stored rollup rather than a recomputation,
so the number here and the number in the list are the same number.

Captured payloads are the whole weight of a trace. A client drawing only a
waterfall should pass bodies=0 and leave them on the server, then fetch the one
record it needs from /traces/{traceId}/records/{id}.

parameters.description: The trace id
parameters.name: traceId

parameters.description: Pass 0 or false to omit the captured payloads. Defaults to including them
parameters.name: bodies

get.description:
One record with its captured payloads, for a client that loaded the trace
with bodies=0 and then opened a single block.

A malformed id answers 404 rather than 400: it addresses no record either
way, and answering alike for "malformed" and "absent" keeps the route from
confirming which ids exist.

parameters.description: The trace id
parameters.name: traceId

parameters.description: The record id, a uuid
parameters.name: id

404.description: no such record, or the id is not a uuid
